h1: The 8 Best Cordless Chainsaws Under $300 for Yard Cleanup and Firewood, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 cordless chainsaws under $300 from EGO, Greenworks, DEWALT and SEESII, scored on voltage, battery watt-hours and bar length.
summary: The EGO POWER+ 16 inch CS1611 is the cordless chainsaw to buy for storm cleanup and light felling, balancing a 56V platform and a 2.5Ah battery at a sensible cost. The CS1613 adds a 4.0Ah battery for longer cuts, the Greenworks 80V 16 inch is a solid value alternative, and the SEESII 40V 16 inch is the cheapest brushless option.
intro: Most first-time buyers compare bar length and ignore the battery, then wonder why a 16 inch saw dies after three logs. A chainsaw is a power-hungry tool, and the figure that predicts run time is watt-hours, not the number of volts on the box. Multiply the voltage by the amp-hours and you get a fair estimate of how much work a charge holds.

This ranking is built around that arithmetic. We reviewed eight cordless saws from their listings: platform voltage, included battery size, bar length, brushless motors where stated and tool-sharing ecosystems. Where a listing gives only a name and a battery size, we work from those and flag what is missing.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1611 16 Inch Chainsaw
products.verdict: A 16 inch, 56V saw with a 2.5Ah battery and charger in the box.
products.description:
The CS1611 is a 16 inch battery chainsaw on EGO's 56V platform, and the kit includes a 2.5Ah battery and a charger. It sits in the $200 to $500 price tier, at the cheaper end for a kit with a battery.

It leads because a 16 inch bar is the size that handles most homeowner tasks, from storm limbs to firewood rounds, and the 56V battery pairs with a large family of EGO tools. A 2.5Ah pack at 56V stores roughly 140 watt-hours, which is enough for a yard cleanup session if you cut in bursts rather than nonstop.

Buy it if you want a dependable all-purpose saw with a battery included. The tradeoff is run time, since a 2.5Ah pack is the smaller option, and you might want to step up to the 4.0Ah kit below for a big job.
pros: Sixteen inch bar suits most jobs
products.idealFor: Homeowners handling storm cleanup and firewood.
products.skipIf: You cut hardwood logs for hours.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1613 16 Inch Chainsaw
products.verdict: The same 16 inch EGO saw with a larger 4.0Ah battery for longer cutting sessions.
products.description:
The CS1613 is a 16 inch EGO POWER+ saw with a 56V 4.0Ah battery and charger. It falls in the $200 to $500 tier, toward the upper end of what this guide covers.

It ranks second because the bigger pack is the one upgrade that most directly changes how the saw feels on a long job. At 56V, a 4.0Ah battery holds about 224 watt-hours, roughly 60 percent more energy than the 2.5Ah kit. You trade that for a higher price and a heavier pack.

Choose it if you have a lot of wood to cut or you hate stopping to swap batteries. If your cutting is occasional, the CS1611 saves money without losing the saw itself.
products.idealFor: People with large wood piles to process.
products.skipIf: You only cut a few limbs a year.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 16 Inch Cordless Chainsaw
products.verdict: An 80V, 16 inch saw with a 2.5Ah battery and charger at a lower tier than EGO.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V is a 16 inch cordless saw with a 2.5Ah battery and a charger, on the 80V platform. It sits in the $200 to $500 tier.

It ranks third because 80V with 2.5Ah stores about 200 watt-hours, which beats the EGO CS1611 on paper, and the bar length is the same. The listing is thinner than the EGO one, with no model number or motor type, so we cannot document the details the way we can for the leaders.

Buy it if you want more battery capacity for your money, or you already own Greenworks 80V tools. Skip it if you want the biggest accessory ecosystem and the most mature dealer support.
products.skipIf: You want the widest accessory range.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 18 Inch Brushless Chainsaw
products.verdict: An 18 inch brushless saw for felling, limbing and firewood, sharing a 75+ tool battery.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V 18 inch is a brushless chainsaw for tree felling, limbing, pruning and firewood, with a 2.0Ah battery and rapid charger. The 80V battery fits more than 75 compatible tools, and it is in the $200 to $500 tier.

It takes fourth place because the larger bar lets you cut thicker trunks in one pass. Brushless motors run cooler and waste less energy than brushed ones, which helps stretch a small battery. The catch is that the 2.0Ah pack, at about 160 watt-hours, is smaller than the packs above, so you will notice run time on larger logs.

It makes sense if you plan to use the battery across a lot of Greenworks gear. Buy a second battery if you cut heavily.
pros: Eighteen inch bar cuts thicker wood
products.idealFor: Greenworks owners wanting more cutting length.
products.skipIf: You want maximum run time per charge.

products.name: DEWALT FLEXVOLT 60V 16 Inch Chainsaw
products.verdict: A 16 inch FLEXVOLT saw with a 2Ah battery on DEWALT's pro-oriented battery platform.
products.description:
The DEWALT FLEXVOLT chainsaw is a 16 inch 60V model sold with a 2Ah battery, in the $200 to $500 tier. FLEXVOLT batteries are designed to work across DEWALT's 20V and 60V tools.

It ranks fifth because the 2Ah battery is on the small side for a saw, and the listing does not publish motor or chain details. What you are buying is the DEWALT platform: contractor-grade dealers, replacement parts and batteries that move between tools.

Buy it if you already own DEWALT batteries and want a saw that joins them. Otherwise, a rival with more battery energy at the same cost is easier to justify.
products.idealFor: DEWALT owners adding a saw to their kit.
products.skipIf: You want the longest run time per dollar.

products.name: SEESII 40V 16 Inch Brushless Chainsaw
products.verdict: The cheapest 16 inch brushless saw here, in the $100 to $200 tier.
products.description:
The SEESII 40V is a 16 inch cordless saw with a brushless motor, and the listing quotes 2000W. It sits in the $100 to $200 tier, the lowest of the 16 inch models.

It ranks sixth because the price is the draw while the brand is less proven than the leaders. Treat a wattage figure on a cordless tool with caution, since it is a peak rating and not a measure of sustained cutting power. A brushless motor still gives better efficiency than the brushed type.

Buy it for occasional yard work on a tight budget. Skip it if you want the backing of a major tool brand.
cons: Wattage claim is a peak figure
products.idealFor: Budget buyers with light cutting needs.
products.skipIf: You want a major tool-brand platform.

products.name: SEESII 40V 18 Inch Chainsaw with Two 5.0Ah Batteries
products.verdict: An 18 inch saw sold with two 5.0Ah batteries, for nonstop cutting on paper.
products.description:
This SEESII is an 18 inch, 40V saw that ships with two 5.0Ah batteries. The listing does not state a price tier, so check the current cost against your budget.

It ranks seventh because two 5.0Ah packs at 40V hold about 200 watt-hours each, which is a lot of cutting for a kit, and the 18 inch bar handles larger limbs. The tradeoff is the same as with the cheaper SEESII: the brand has less track record, and warranty and parts availability matter on a tool you may rely on.

It is a good choice if run time is your priority and you want a spare pack for swapping. Be careful about heft, since a long bar with a large battery is tiring to hold overhead.
pros: Eighteen inch bar cuts bigger limbs
products.idealFor: People who want long run time and a spare battery.
products.skipIf: You want a brand with deep service support.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1201 12 Inch Chainsaw
products.verdict: A light 12 inch EGO saw with a 2.5Ah battery for pruning and small limbs.
products.description:
The CS1201 is a 12 inch battery chainsaw on the 56V EGO platform, with a 2.5Ah battery and charger. It sits in the $200 to $500 tier.

It ranks last because the short bar limits cut diameter, and a 12 inch saw is closer to a pruning tool than a felling saw. What you gain is lighter weight and easier handling, which helps with overhead branches and tight spaces.

Buy it for trimming, small limbs and kindling. If you plan to cut anything thicker than a thigh, step up to a 16 inch model instead.
products.skipIf: You cut thick logs or whole trees.

methodology.title: Battery energy
methodology.description: We multiplied voltage by amp-hours to estimate watt-hours per pack, since that figure predicts run time better than voltage alone.

methodology.title: Bar length and cut size
methodology.description: Bar length was matched to the jobs homeowners actually do, from pruning with 12 inches to firewood with 16 and 18.

methodology.title: Motor and platform
methodology.description: Brushless motors, platform voltage and the number of compatible tools on the same battery were credited.

methodology.title: What is in the box
methodology.description: Kits that include a battery and charger, or a second battery, scored higher than bare tools.

methodology.title: Value under $300
methodology.description: Each saw was judged on documented capability against its price tier, with thin listings marked down.

whatMatters.detail: Volts times amp-hours gives watt-hours, the real size of the fuel tank. A 56V 2.5Ah pack holds about 140 watt-hours and a 56V 4.0Ah pack about 224. Compare that figure across brands rather than amp-hours alone, since a 40V 5.0Ah pack and a 56V 4.0Ah pack are close in energy.

The usable cut is a couple of inches shorter than the bar, so a 16 inch bar cuts roughly a 14 inch log. Longer bars add weight and strain a small battery. Choose the shortest bar that handles your thickest regular job.

Brushless motors waste less energy as heat and last longer than brushed ones, which stretches battery life. Not every listing states the motor type, so look for the word brushless. Be wary of peak wattage claims, which say little about sustained cutting.

A saw on the same battery as your trimmer, mower or blower saves money on extra packs. Platforms like EGO 56V, Greenworks 80V and DEWALT FLEXVOLT each cover dozens of tools. Check the ecosystem before you buy so the battery works with tools you may add later.

A chain brake, a low-kickback chain and a tensioning system are basic safety features, and chain oil and sharpening keep the saw cutting well. A dull chain strains the motor and the battery. Check for oil reservoir details, a chain brake and replacement chain availability.

faq.q: Can a cordless chainsaw replace a gas saw?
faq.a: For homeowner tasks such as limbs, storm cleanup and firewood, yes. For all-day felling of large trees, a gas saw still runs longer.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with a cordless saw?
faq.a: Skipping chain oil or running a dull chain, which wears the bar and drains the battery. Fill the oil reservoir before every session and sharpen the chain often.

faq.q: Is a bigger battery worth it?
faq.a: If you cut for longer than half an hour at a time, yes, since the stored energy directly sets run time. For occasional jobs a smaller pack saves money.

faq.q: How do I set up a new saw?
faq.a: Fit the bar and chain, set the chain tension so it lifts slightly off the bar, fill the oil reservoir and charge the battery fully. Check the tension again after the first few cuts.

faq.q: How should I store the saw and battery?
faq.a: Keep the battery indoors at moderate temperature, with the bar cover fitted and the oil drained if you will not use it for months. Avoid leaving batteries in a hot garage.

faq.q: What safety gear do I need?
faq.a: Chainsaw chaps, eye and ear protection, gloves and sturdy boots are the minimum. Never cut above shoulder height with a full-size saw.

finalTake: Buy the EGO POWER+ CS1611 for a balanced cordless saw that handles most yard jobs, and step up to the CS1613 if you cut for long stretches. The Greenworks 80V 16 inch is the value alternative, and the SEESII 40V 16 inch is the cheapest brushless option for light use. Skip the 12 inch saw unless pruning is the only job on your list.
